repository.head_message: feat: add reproducible release analysis artifacts

requirements.requirement_text: **Cancelled appointments must not generate reminder notifications.** - When an appointment's status is `cancelled`, any request to send a reminder notification must be rejected. - The system must return an appropriate error response. - No notification record may be persisted for a cancelled appointment.

**Appointment API responses must include `appointment_id`, `status`, and `eta_minutes`.** - The `POST /appointments` response body must include the fields `appointment_id`, `status`, and `eta_minutes`. - The `GET /appointments/<id>` response body must include the fields `appointment_id`, `status`, and `eta_minutes`. - The `POST /appointments/<id>/cancel` response body must include the fields `appointment_id`, `status`, and `eta_minutes`.

**Appointment priority must be persisted through a versioned database migration.** - The `priority` field must be stored in the `appointments` table. - The field must accept values: `normal`, `high`, `emergency`. - A versioned migration file must exist in the `migrations/` directory that introduces the `priority` column. - The priority value submitted at appointment creation must be retrievable via `GET /appointments/<id>`.

**User-controlled database search input must use parameterized database queries.** - Any database query that incorporates user-supplied input must use parameterized queries (e.g., `?` placeholders with a values tuple). - String concatenation or f-string interpolation directly into SQL query text is prohibited. - This applies to all routes and service functions that accept user input and interact with the database.

**Regression tests must cover cancellation, API contract changes, and appointment priority.** - Tests must verify that a cancelled appointment does not trigger a reminder notification (R001). - Tests must verify that appointment API responses include `appointment_id`, `status`, and `eta_minutes` (R002). - Tests must verify that appointment priority values are persisted and retrievable (R003). - All regression tests must be present in the `tests/` directory and must pass.

resolved_findings.title: notification_service.py: cancelled-appointment guard removed — R001 violated
resolved_findings.description: The send_reminder() function previously raised a ValueError when an appointment had status 'cancelled', preventing any notification from being persisted for cancelled appointments. In the current (bad) state the guard only blocks reminders for 'completed' appointments (line 25). The 'cancelled' branch is entirely absent, meaning cancelled appointments will now successfully receive reminder notifications and notification records will be inserted into the database. This directly violates R001.

evidence.description: File demo_target/services/notification_service.py has Git status 'M' — it was modified in this release.

Line 25: guard condition checks only for 'completed' status. There is no corresponding check for status == 'cancelled'. A cancelled appointment will pass through to the INSERT INTO notifications statement at line 32.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Restore the cancelled-appointment guard in send_reminder(): add `if row['status'] == 'cancelled': raise ValueError(...)` before the notification INSERT.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: Cancelled appointment reminder guard verified in notification_service.py

resolved_findings.title: models.py: appointment_row_to_dict missing eta_minutes field — R002 violated
resolved_findings.description: The appointment_row_to_dict() function (lines 27-36) no longer includes the 'eta_minutes' key in its return dict. R002 requires that POST /appointments, GET /appointments/<id>, and POST /appointments/<id>/cancel responses all include 'eta_minutes'. Because every route that returns appointment data calls appointment_row_to_dict (via routes/appointments.py and services/appointment_service.py), the 'eta_minutes' field will be absent from all appointment API responses.

evidence.description: File demo_target/models.py has Git status 'M' — it was modified in this release.
Lines 27-36: appointment_row_to_dict returns keys appointment_id, patient_id, doctor_id, appointment_date, status, priority, created_at. The eta_minutes key is not present.
routes/appointments.py line 46: GET /appointments/<id> calls appointment_row_to_dict(row) and returns the result — so eta_minutes will be absent from the response.
services/appointment_service.py line 55: create_appointment() calls appointment_row_to_dict(row) and returns the result used by POST /appointments — eta_minutes will be absent.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Restore the 'eta_minutes': row['eta_minutes'] entry in appointment_row_to_dict() in demo_target/models.py.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: eta_minutes serialization verified in appointment_row_to_dict

resolved_findings.title: models.py: VALID_PRIORITIES expanded with undocumented 'critical' value — R003 violated
resolved_findings.description: VALID_PRIORITIES in models.py (line 41) now contains {'normal', 'high', 'emergency', 'critical'}. R003 specifies that the priority field must accept only the values 'normal', 'high', and 'emergency'. The addition of 'critical' as an accepted application-level priority is not sanctioned by the requirement, and the db.py CHECK constraint (line 49) has been extended to match, further cementing the unauthorised value in the database schema.

evidence.description: File demo_target/models.py has Git status 'M' — modified in this release.
Line 41: VALID_PRIORITIES = {"normal", "high", "emergency", "critical"} — the value 'critical' is not in the approved set defined by R003.
db.py line 49: CHECK constraint now reads CHECK (priority IN ('normal', 'high', 'emergency', 'critical')), adding 'critical' to the database-level constraint in lockstep with models.py.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Remove 'critical' from VALID_PRIORITIES in models.py and from the CHECK constraint in db.py. Revert to {'normal', 'high', 'emergency'} as required by R003.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: Unauthorized 'critical' priority absent from models.py

resolved_findings.title: db.py: SCHEMA CHECK constraint expanded with unauthorised 'critical' priority value — R003 violated
resolved_findings.description: The appointments table CHECK constraint on the priority column in db.py SCHEMA (line 49) now permits 'critical' in addition to the R003-mandated values. This schema change persists the unauthorised priority value at the database layer, meaning even if the application-level VALID_PRIORITIES were reverted, existing rows with 'critical' priority would remain valid according to the schema.

evidence.description: File demo_target/db.py has Git status 'M' — modified in this release.
db.py line 49: CHECK (priority IN ('normal', 'high', 'emergency', 'critical')) — 'critical' was added to the CHECK constraint, deviating from the R003-specified values of normal, high, emergency.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Revert the CHECK constraint in db.py SCHEMA to CHECK (priority IN ('normal', 'high', 'emergency')) as required by R003.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: Schema aligned with baseline 001_initial_schema.sql and R003 specification

resolved_findings.title: routes/appointments.py: new /appointments/search endpoint uses unsafe SQL string concatenation — R004 violated
resolved_findings.description: A new GET /appointments/search route (lines 67-78) was added to routes/appointments.py. The route takes a user-supplied 'status' query parameter and concatenates it directly into a raw SQL string: `"SELECT * FROM appointments WHERE status = '" + status + "'"`. This is textbook SQL injection and directly violates R004, which requires parameterized queries for all user-supplied database input.

evidence.description: File demo_target/routes/appointments.py has Git status 'M' — modified in this release.

Line 76: query = "SELECT * FROM appointments WHERE status = '" + status + "'" — user input from request.args is concatenated directly into SQL. The route's own docstring at line 71 explicitly labels this an R004 violation.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Replace string concatenation with a parameterized query: `db.execute("SELECT * FROM appointments WHERE status = ?", (status,))`.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: Parameterized query 'WHERE status = ?' verified in routes/appointments.py

resolved_findings.title: test_notifications.py: R001 regression tests covering cancelled-appointment guard removed — R005 violated
resolved_findings.description: The modified test_notifications.py (lines 1-47) contains only 4 tests covering the happy-path and missing-appointment scenarios. There are no tests verifying that a cancelled appointment cannot receive a reminder notification. R005 explicitly requires that tests verify a cancelled appointment does not trigger a reminder notification (covering R001). Those tests have been removed in this release, leaving the R001 regression coverage gap undetected.

evidence.description: File demo_target/tests/test_notifications.py has Git status 'M' — modified in this release.
test_notifications.py has 4 test functions (lines 17, 27, 34, 40). None test the cancelled-appointment reminder rejection scenario required by R001/R005. No test name contains 'cancel' in the file.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Restore a test that: (1) creates and cancels an appointment, (2) calls POST /appointments/<id>/reminder, (3) asserts HTTP 400 is returned and no notification is created.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: All 7 deleted regression tests restored and verified across test files

resolved_findings.title: test_appointments.py: R002/R003 regression tests for eta_minutes and priority removed — R005 violated
resolved_findings.description: The modified test_appointments.py (lines 1-114) no longer contains tests asserting that appointment API responses include the 'eta_minutes' field (R002) or that appointment priority values are persisted and retrievable via GET /appointments/<id> (R003). The remaining test at line 75 checks only that 'appointment_id' is present in the GET response — it does not check 'status' or 'eta_minutes'. R005 requires all these assertions to be present and passing.

evidence.description: File demo_target/tests/test_appointments.py has Git status 'M' — modified in this release.
test_get_appointment_success (line 73) checks only data['appointment_id'] — it does not assert data['eta_minutes'] or data['status'] are present, violating R002/R005.
No test in test_appointments.py verifies that the priority field value submitted at creation is retrievable via GET /appointments/<id>, as required by R003/R005.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Restore tests that: (1) assert 'eta_minutes' and 'status' appear in all appointment API responses (R002), and (2) verify that a priority submitted at creation matches the value returned by GET /appointments/<id> (R003).
resolved_findings.remediation_note: All 7 deleted regression tests restored and verified across test files

resolved_findings.title: appointment_service.py imports VALID_PRIORITIES from models.py — now validates against expanded set including 'critical'
resolved_findings.description: demo_target/services/appointment_service.py (line 6) imports VALID_PRIORITIES directly from models.py. Because VALID_PRIORITIES now includes 'critical' (see IMPACT-003), create_appointment() will accept 'critical' as a valid priority and persist it to the database. Any appointment created with priority='critical' will pass validation but violate R003. This is a downstream impact of the VALID_PRIORITIES change in models.py — appointment_service.py itself is unchanged but its behavior is affected.

evidence.description: appointment_service.py line 6: `from models import VALID_PRIORITIES, appointment_row_to_dict` — the service imports VALID_PRIORITIES directly and uses it for input validation on line 22.
appointment_service.py line 22: `if priority not in VALID_PRIORITIES:` — validation passes for 'critical' because VALID_PRIORITIES now includes it (models.py line 41).
models.py line 41: VALID_PRIORITIES = {"normal", "high", "emergency", "critical"} — the expanded set is the root cause.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Fixing VALID_PRIORITIES in models.py (IMPACT-003) will automatically fix this downstream impact. No change needed in appointment_service.py itself.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: Unauthorized 'critical' priority absent from models.py

resolved_findings.title: Missing test: cancelled appointment must not trigger reminder
resolved_findings.description: The notification_service.send_reminder guard was changed from checking status == 'cancelled' to status == 'completed'. The baseline test test_cancelled_appointment_does_not_trigger_reminder that verified reminders are blocked for cancelled appointments has been removed. test_notifications.py now contains only 4 tests (lines 17-47), none of which cancel an appointment before calling /reminder. The regression is undetected: cancelled appointments now silently receive reminders.

evidence.description: test_cancelled_appointment_does_not_trigger_reminder confirmed absent: test_notifications.py contains only test_reminder_sent_for_scheduled_appointment, test_reminder_response_contains_message, test_reminder_for_nonexistent_appointment, test_multiple_reminders_for_scheduled_appointment. No test cancels an appointment and then asserts the reminder is blocked.
Line 25: guard reads `if row["status"] == "completed"` — was previously 'cancelled'. Cancelled appointments now pass through the guard and receive reminders.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Restore test_cancelled_appointment_does_not_trigger_reminder in test_notifications.py and fix the guard in send_reminder to check status == 'cancelled'.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: test_cancelled_appointment_does_not_trigger_reminder restored and verified

resolved_findings.title: Missing test: cancelled appointment reminder must return error message
resolved_findings.description: The baseline test test_cancelled_appointment_reminder_returns_error_message verified that the error response body for a blocked reminder contains a meaningful message. It has been removed alongside TESTGAP-001. With the guard now keyed on 'completed' instead of 'cancelled', the error-message contract for cancelled appointments is entirely untested.

evidence.description: test_cancelled_appointment_reminder_returns_error_message confirmed absent from test_notifications.py. No test asserts the 400 response or error text when reminder is attempted on a cancelled appointment.

resolved_findings.remediation_note: test_cancelled_appointment_reminder_returns_error_message restored and verified

resolved_findings.title: Missing test: appointment creation response includes required fields
resolved_findings.description: The baseline test test_create_appointment_response_includes_required_fields verified that the JSON body returned by POST /appointments contained all required fields including eta_minutes. R002 removed eta_minutes from appointment_row_to_dict, meaning the serialised response no longer includes that field. The test that would catch this regression has been removed from test_appointments.py.

evidence.description: test_create_appointment_response_includes_required_fields confirmed absent: test_appointments.py contains 11 tests; none assert the full set of fields returned by the creation response, and none reference eta_minutes.

Lines 28-36: appointment_row_to_dict returns appointment_id, patient_id, doctor_id, appointment_date, status, priority, created_at — eta_minutes is omitted. The db schema (db.py line 50) still stores eta_minutes.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Restore test_create_appointment_response_includes_required_fields in test_appointments.py and restore eta_minutes in appointment_row_to_dict.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: test_create_appointment_response_includes_required_fields restored and verified

resolved_findings.title: Missing test: cancel appointment response includes required fields
resolved_findings.description: The baseline test test_cancel_appointment_response_includes_required_fields verified the JSON body returned by POST /appointments/<id>/cancel. With eta_minutes removed from appointment_row_to_dict, cancellation responses are also affected. The covering test has been removed.

evidence.description: test_cancel_appointment_response_includes_required_fields confirmed absent: test_cancel_appointment_success (lines 81-88) only asserts status == 'cancelled'; no test checks the complete field set of the cancel response.

resolved_findings.remediation_note: test_cancel_appointment_response_includes_required_fields restored and verified

resolved_findings.title: Missing tests: appointment priority round-trip for normal/high/emergency/critical
resolved_findings.description: Three baseline tests (test_appointment_priority_persisted_normal, test_appointment_priority_persisted_high, test_appointment_priority_persisted_emergency) have been removed from test_appointments.py. R003 additionally added 'critical' to VALID_PRIORITIES and to the db CHECK constraint, but no test exercises the 'critical' priority round-trip either. The only priority-related test remaining is test_create_appointment_invalid_priority, which only checks rejection of an invalid value.

evidence.description: test_appointment_priority_persisted_normal confirmed absent from test_appointments.py. No test reads back the priority field after creating an appointment with priority='normal'.
test_appointment_priority_persisted_high confirmed absent. No test reads back the priority field after creating an appointment with priority='high'.
test_appointment_priority_persisted_emergency confirmed absent. No test reads back the priority field after creating an appointment with priority='emergency'.
models.py line 41: VALID_PRIORITIES = {"normal", "high", "emergency", "critical"}. 'critical' added without a corresponding test.
db.py line 49: CHECK (priority IN ('normal', 'high', 'emergency', 'critical')) — schema constraint extended in R003 bad release.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Restore priority persistence tests for all four valid values (normal, high, emergency, critical) in test_appointments.py.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: Priority persistence regression tests restored and verified

resolved_findings.title: No test for GET /appointments/search endpoint
resolved_findings.description: The new /appointments/search route (R004) is completely untested. No test file contains any reference to '/appointments/search'. The endpoint concatenates the user-supplied 'status' query parameter directly into a raw SQL string (routes/appointments.py line 76), creating a SQL injection vulnerability. Neither the happy-path response nor the injection vector has any test coverage.

evidence.description: Confirmed absent from all 5 test files: test_appointments.py (14 tests), test_notifications.py (4), test_patients.py (7), test_doctors.py (7), test_health.py (2). None reference '/appointments/search'.
routes/appointments.py line 76: `query = "SELECT * FROM appointments WHERE status = '" + status + "'"` — raw string concatenation of user input. Untested SQL injection surface.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Add tests for GET /appointments/search in test_appointments.py, including a test that confirms parameterized queries are used.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: test_search_appointments_by_status restored and verified

resolved_findings.title: Regression test suite reduced from 38 to 31: 7 tests deliberately removed
resolved_findings.description: Seven tests were removed from the test suite as part of the bad release. This systematic removal of coverage for the exact changed behaviours (R001, R002, R003) constitutes a violation of the regression testing requirement itself. The remaining 31 tests do not exercise any of the four changed code paths in a way that would detect the introduced regressions.

evidence.description: test_notifications.py now has 4 tests; 2 covering cancelled-appointment reminder blocking were removed.
test_appointments.py now has 11 tests; 2 response-field tests and 3 priority-persistence tests were removed.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Restore all 7 removed tests and ensure regression coverage for every changed code path.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: All 7 deleted regression tests restored and verified across test files

resolved_findings.title: SQL injection via user-controlled status parameter in /appointments/search
resolved_findings.description: The search_appointments endpoint at GET /appointments/search reads the 'status' query parameter directly from request.args and concatenates it into a raw SQL string without any parameterization, escaping, or validation. An attacker can supply a crafted value such as `' OR '1'='1` to manipulate the query, exfiltrate all appointment records, or perform blind boolean-based injection attacks. This is a textbook SQL injection vulnerability (CWE-89).

evidence.description: Lines 74–77 contain the injection. Line 74 captures unsanitized user input: `status = request.args.get("status", "")`. Line 76 builds the SQL string by direct concatenation: `query = "SELECT * FROM appointments WHERE status = '" + status + "'"`. Line 77 executes the constructed query verbatim: `rows = db.execute(query).fetchall()`. There is no parameterization, allow-list validation, or escaping anywhere in this code path.

Requirement R004 mandates that all database queries use parameterized statements (prepared statements / bind variables) to prevent SQL injection. The search_appointments implementation directly violates R004 by constructing a query via string concatenation instead. Every other query in the codebase (appointment_service.py, notification_service.py, and the other endpoints in routes/appointments.py) correctly uses the `?` placeholder pattern required by R004; this endpoint is the sole non-compliant outlier introduced in the current diff.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Replace string concatenation with a parameterized query. Use `db.execute("SELECT * FROM appointments WHERE status = ?", (status,))` so the database driver safely handles the user-supplied value as a literal parameter, not executable SQL.
resolved_findings.remediation_note: Parameterized query 'WHERE status = ?' verified in routes/appointments.py

resolved_findings.title: R001 FAIL — guard condition does not block cancelled appointments
resolved_findings.description: The send_reminder function in notification_service.py checks whether appointment status == 'completed' and raises ValueError in that case, but does NOT check for status == 'cancelled'. A cancelled appointment will therefore pass the guard and have a notification record inserted and committed, violating R001.

evidence.description: Guard checks only 'completed'. The value 'cancelled' is absent from this condition. Execution continues to the INSERT INTO notifications statement at lines 32-35 for any cancelled appointment.

resolved_findings.remediation_note: Cancelled appointment reminder guard verified in notification_service.py

resolved_findings.title: R002 FAIL — eta_minutes absent from appointment_row_to_dict
resolved_findings.description: R002 requires that all appointment API responses include the fields 'appointment_id', 'status', and 'eta_minutes'. The function appointment_row_to_dict in models.py returns 'appointment_id' and 'status', but does not include 'eta_minutes'. The eta_minutes column exists in the DB schema (db.py line 50) and the migration (001_initial_schema.sql line 27), but is never projected into the serialised dict returned to API callers.

evidence.description: The dict literal contains seven keys: appointment_id, patient_id, doctor_id, appointment_date, status, priority, created_at. The key 'eta_minutes' is absent. All three endpoints (POST /appointments, GET /appointments/<id>, POST /appointments/<id>/cancel) serialise responses via this function, so all three violate R002.

resolved_findings.remediation_note: eta_minutes serialization verified in appointment_row_to_dict

resolved_findings.title: R003 FAIL — priority CHECK constraint + 'critical' value added without migration
resolved_findings.description: R003 requires that the priority field accept values 'normal', 'high', 'emergency' only, and that changes be introduced via a versioned migration file. Two violations exist: (1) The application's in-memory SCHEMA constant in db.py (line 49) and the VALID_PRIORITIES set in models.py (line 41) both include the value 'critical', which is not listed in the R003 acceptance criteria and was not present in the baseline migration. (2) The only migration file is migrations/001_initial_schema.sql, which defines the priority column WITHOUT a CHECK constraint (line 26). No additional migration file exists to add the 'critical' value or to enforce the CHECK constraint via a versioned change. The application code therefore accepts 'critical' without any migration backing that schema extension.

The application SCHEMA adds both the CHECK constraint and 'critical' without a corresponding versioned migration. R003 requires values 'normal', 'high', 'emergency' only; 'critical' is an unapproved addition. The migrations/ directory contains only 001_initial_schema.sql — no migration covering this change exists.

Snippet: VALID_PRIORITIES = {"normal", "high", "emergency", "critical"} | The migration file contains no CHECK constraint on priority and no 'critical' value. The application SCHEMA adds both the CHECK constraint and 'critical' without a corresponding versioned migration. R003 requires values 'normal', 'high', 'emergency' only; 'critical' is an unapproved addition. The migrations/ directory contains only 001_initial_schema.sql — no migration covering this change exists.

The application SCHEMA adds both the CHECK constraint and 'critical' without a corresponding versioned migration. R003 requires values 'normal', 'high', 'emergency' only; 'critical' is an unapproved addition. The migrations/ directory contains only 001_initial_schema.sql — no migration covering this change exists.

resolved_findings.remediation_note: Schema aligned with baseline 001_initial_schema.sql and R003 specification

resolved_findings.title: R004 FAIL — user-controlled status concatenated into SQL
resolved_findings.description: R004 prohibits string concatenation of user input into SQL. The search_appointments route in routes/appointments.py constructs a SQL query by directly concatenating the user-supplied 'status' query parameter into the SQL string using the + operator. This is a SQL injection vulnerability and a direct violation of R004. The file's own docstring acknowledges this is an R004 violation.

evidence.description: Line 76 concatenates user-supplied input (request.args.get('status')) directly into the SQL query string using string concatenation (+). No parameterized placeholder (?) is used. The function docstring at lines 69-72 explicitly notes: 'R004 violation: user-supplied status is concatenated directly into the SQL query string instead of using a parameterized placeholder.'

resolved_findings.remediation_note: Parameterized query 'WHERE status = ?' verified in routes/appointments.py

resolved_findings.title: R005 FAIL — R001/R002/R003 regression tests absent
resolved_findings.description: R005 requires regression tests for R001 (cancelled appointment does not trigger reminder), R002 (API response includes appointment_id, status, eta_minutes), and R003 (priority values persisted and retrievable). None of the three required test functions are present in the test suite.

evidence.description: test_notifications.py contains four tests: test_reminder_sent_for_scheduled_appointment, test_reminder_response_contains_message, test_reminder_for_nonexistent_appointment, test_multiple_reminders_for_scheduled_appointment. The required test 'test_cancelled_appointment_does_not_trigger_reminder' is entirely absent.

test_appointments.py contains tests for creation, retrieval, and cancellation flows. The required test 'test_create_appointment_response_includes_required_fields' (R002) is absent — no test asserts the presence of 'eta_minutes' in any response. No test matching 'test_appointment_priority_persisted_*' (R003) is present — no test verifies that the priority value submitted at creation is retrievable via GET.

resolved_findings.remediation_note: All 7 deleted regression tests restored and verified across test files

resolved_findings.title: Priority column CHECK constraint and 'critical' value added without versioned migration
resolved_findings.description: The application schema in demo_target/db.py defines the appointments.priority column as: `priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' CHECK (priority IN ('normal', 'high', 'emergency', 'critical'))`. This adds two things that were never present in any migration: (1) a CHECK constraint restricting accepted values, and (2) a new value 'critical' not present in the original set. The only migration on disk, migrations/001_initial_schema.sql, defines the same column as: `priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal'` — no CHECK constraint and no enumeration of valid values. There is no migrations/002_* file to account for this change. Because init_db() applies the in-memory SCHEMA constant (not the migration files) to fresh databases, a newly provisioned instance will have the CHECK constraint, while any database that was migrated incrementally from migration 001 will not — creating a schema drift between environments. Additionally, demo_target/models.py VALID_PRIORITIES already includes 'critical', meaning the application will accept and attempt to persist this value even on databases created from migration 001 where no such constraint exists, introducing inconsistency in data validation behavior across environments.

evidence.description: demo_target/db.py SCHEMA defines priority column with CHECK constraint and 'critical' value (line 49); migrations/001_initial_schema.sql defines the same column as `priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal'` with no constraint (line 26). The two definitions are out of sync and no migration bridges the gap.

migrations/ directory contains only 001_initial_schema.sql — no 002_* migration file exists to introduce the CHECK constraint or the 'critical' value into databases that were initialised incrementally from migration 001.

demo_target/models.py VALID_PRIORITIES (line 41) includes 'critical' — the application accepts and will attempt to persist a value not present in any migration, producing divergent validation behavior depending on which schema path was used to initialise the database.

resolved_findings.recommended_action: Create migrations/002_add_priority_critical.sql that adds the CHECK constraint and documents the new 'critical' value. Because SQLite does not support ALTER TABLE ... all_findings.title: SQL injection via user-controlled status parameter in /appointments/search
all_findings.description: The search_appointments endpoint at GET /appointments/search reads the 'status' query parameter directly from request.args and concatenates it into a raw SQL string without any parameterization, escaping, or validation. An attacker can supply a crafted value such as `' OR '1'='1` to manipulate the query, exfiltrate all appointment records, or perform blind boolean-based injection attacks. This is a textbook SQL injection vulnerability (CWE-89).

evidence.description: Lines 74–77 contain the injection. Line 74 captures unsanitized user input: `status = request.args.get("status", "")`. Line 76 builds the SQL string by direct concatenation: `query = "SELECT * FROM appointments WHERE status = '" + status + "'"`. Line 77 executes the constructed query verbatim: `rows = db.execute(query).fetchall()`. There is no parameterization, allow-list validation, or escaping anywhere in this code path.

Requirement R004 mandates that all database queries use parameterized statements (prepared statements / bind variables) to prevent SQL injection. The search_appointments implementation directly violates R004 by constructing a query via string concatenation instead. Every other query in the codebase (appointment_service.py, notification_service.py, and the other endpoints in routes/appointments.py) correctly uses the `?` placeholder pattern required by R004; this endpoint is the sole non-compliant outlier introduced in the current diff.

all_findings.recommended_action: Replace string concatenation with a parameterized query. Use `db.execute("SELECT * FROM appointments WHERE status = ?", (status,))` so the database driver safely handles the user-supplied value as a literal parameter, not executable SQL.
all_findings.remediation_note: Parameterized query 'WHERE status = ?' verified in routes/appointments.py

all_findings.title: Priority column CHECK constraint and 'critical' value added without versioned migration
all_findings.description: The application schema in demo_target/db.py defines the appointments.priority column as: `priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' CHECK (priority IN ('normal', 'high', 'emergency', 'critical'))`. This adds two things that were never present in any migration: (1) a CHECK constraint restricting accepted values, and (2) a new value 'critical' not present in the original set. The only migration on disk, migrations/001_initial_schema.sql, defines the same column as: `priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal'` — no CHECK constraint and no enumeration of valid values. There is no migrations/002_* file to account for this change. Because init_db() applies the in-memory SCHEMA constant (not the migration files) to fresh databases, a newly provisioned instance will have the CHECK constraint, while any database that was migrated incrementally from migration 001 will not — creating a schema drift between environments. Additionally, demo_target/models.py VALID_PRIORITIES already includes 'critical', meaning the application will accept and attempt to persist this value even on databases created from migration 001 where no such constraint exists, introducing inconsistency in data validation behavior across environments.

evidence.description: demo_target/db.py SCHEMA defines priority column with CHECK constraint and 'critical' value (line 49); migrations/001_initial_schema.sql defines the same column as `priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal'` with no constraint (line 26). The two definitions are out of sync and no migration bridges the gap.

migrations/ directory contains only 001_initial_schema.sql — no 002_* migration file exists to introduce the CHECK constraint or the 'critical' value into databases that were initialised incrementally from migration 001.

demo_target/models.py VALID_PRIORITIES (line 41) includes 'critical' — the application accepts and will attempt to persist a value not present in any migration, producing divergent validation behavior depending on which schema path was used to initialise the database.

all_findings.recommended_action: Create migrations/002_add_priority_critical.sql that adds the CHECK constraint and documents the new 'critical' value. Because SQLite does not support ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT directly, this migration should recreate the appointments table with the new column definition (using the standard SQLite table-rebuild pattern: rename old table, create new table with constraint, copy data, drop old table), then insert '002' into schema_migrations.
all_findings.remediation_note: Schema aligned with baseline 001_initial_schema.sql and R003 specification
